title: Strategic Residential Location Choice: How Parents Game Priorities in School Matching
eligible_reason: Pooled OLS on child-month registration data: return move on application-age x first-half-of-school-year interaction (Equation (2), Tables 2-4) with only the two main effects and a linear age term; no child fixed effects (author states they cannot be estimated) and no calendar-time fixed effects (the event, the February application deadline, is common to all children every year). The 'panel event study' (Equation (1), Figures 3-4) indexes calendar months relative to February with school-year FE and is likewise common timing. Not a staggered-adoption design with unit and time FE.
design_notes: 02_analysis.do: reg rmove1000 i.appl_agey##i.firsthalf [age_m_norm] [##i.migrant ##i.famnonaca], cluster(zmrid) (Table 2); Table 3 adds school-reform interactions (single reform date, school years 2019+); Table 4 interacts with continuous district characteristics; probit robustness; Table 5 survey OLS.
data_files_note: City of Vienna registration panel (child-month, ~303,000 children) restricted to the variables needed for the paper; parent survey.
data_provenance_note: Administrative data restricted to needed variables, full population of children aged 4-11.
screener_notes: Published PDF text read (data/text/mnsc/mnsc.2021.03711.txt). Treatment (application age x first half) switches on and off by age; no unit FE in any column, so not recorded as a near-miss.
